messages.content:
My  experience with PM Screening Interviews with Meta. 

Did ***not** get selected for the onsite but maybe my experience can help.

First off, they just ask you the questions you’d expect!
The Product Sense interview asked me to design products.
The Product Execution interview asked me to set goals.

1. 1.    I think to start with - get your resume reviewed at #resume-review.
2. 2.    Get a referral from #referrals 
3. 3.    Give yourself time to Prep!
4. 4.    Have a framework for each type of question

Books I read: [Not necessary]
•    The Product Manager Interview
•    Decode and Conquer
•    Cracking the PM Interview
•    The Managers Path

Trainings:
Not affiliated 
 •    TryExponent.com
 •    Stellar Peers
 •    Lewis Lin Stuff
I applied for a generic position that required 3 years of experience.
The Meta recruiter reached out and set a time over email.
First discussion included discussing my experience and an overview of the interview process.
Recruiter was professional and polished, gave me exactly what I needed and nothing else.
No discussion of Band or Money. Meta Product Manager Interviews are to verify general fit first.
Very progressive 

Meta then sent a calendar and access to a portal where everything was tracked. I picked a date a month out.
Video interviews set back-to-back one day with an hour in between [probably interviewer selected]. Third interview next day.

Product Sense Interviews: [45 Minutes Each]
 •    Design Library [Similar]
 •    Design a Meditation App [Similar]
Product Execution: [45 Minutes]
 •    You are a PM for Instagram. What are your Goals? [Similar question]

I can talk a little more about the format I used if there is any interest but there are a ton of answers for these out there.

How my google interview went 
A recruiter reached out to me asking if I’m interested in a Product Manager role for GCP. I said sure, we had the initial recruiter call and she said to go straight to on-site loop, no need for a phone screen. I had been interviewing before now but I knew google PM interview was different so I booked my loop 3 weeks in advance.
To prepare, I subscribed for try exponent course - compared to the product alliance course, this was more useful with practical steps and had more substance. (Also it’s good value for money, compared to product alliance) I invested at least 4hrs a day for 21days to prepare. First 2 weeks was just for reading and coming up with  frameworks, the 3rd week was purely for practicing. Paying it forward and sharing my interview experience: 
Interview 1- [product insight/strategy] - 
Question 1- imagine we had a self driving technology, build a taxi app for the blind. We have no legal constraints, what would you build. She then proceeded to ask about pricing, GTM and metrics. 
Question 2- we’ve built a battery that can go 100yrs without recharge, let’s brainstorm on the use cases and personas.
Interview 2 [analytical/cross functional] 
Question 1- tell me your favourite product and build a 1 year roadmap for it. Proceeded to ask about metrics and GTM
Question 2- you have unlimited data from a users phone, how would you deduce the time the user slept and woke up. 
Interview 3 [product insight /craft & execution]
Question 1- you have all the geolocation data from the past 20yrs, what would you build 
Question 2- when I go on vacation and return I get overwhelmed with multiple slack messages and notifications. You’re the PM how would you solve for this and help users prioritize what messages to read.
Interview 4 [strategic/googlyness/leadership]
Question 1- competing engineering priorities, how do you deal with it
Question 2- 3 leadership qualities I’ve seen in leaders I admire, how have I incorporated that into my PM life

Interview 5 [sub domain questions - craft&execution/cross functional] 
Question 1 - behavioural 
Question 2 - GTM strategy 
 
General advice - have a framework and stick to it. Ask questions, take pauses. Ask for time to think. The try exponent course is really good if you don’t know where to start from. Also checkout Dianna Yau on YouTube, you can pick a thing or two from her channel.

Thank you both. So what's the framework you'd use for: 

"[product insight / craft & execution] Question 2- when I go on vacation and return I get overwhelmed with multiple slack messages and notifications. You’re the PM how would you solve for this and help users prioritize what messages to read."?

Is something like below in the ballpark?
- Clarify the Q, assumptions and any constraints
- Set a goal + user value we're optimizing for while considering different user segments
- Propose some solutions and pick one based on trade-offs
- Talk about how you'd test the solution / validate
Sounds reasonable to me. Perhaps touch on Business Objectives and Success Metrics as well.
